newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Last rate cut not fully through - Costello.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Last rate cut not fully through - Costello.

text.p: Australian Treasurer Peter Costello said on Wednesday the effects of the last reduction in official interest rates in May were yet to fully flow through to the business community.
"The interest rate cut in May was a reward for low inflation and an improving budgetary situation," Costello said.
"The effect of that is still I believe to fully flow through into the business community," he said.
Costello repeated his criticism of some banks which he said had not passed on in full the most recent rate cut to all customers.
Official cash interest rates, now at 5.5 percent, have been cut four times since July last year, the last cut being on May 23.

Analysts and financial markets are widely expecting another cut in interest rates after today's inflation data and Thursday's second quarter wages figures. The Reserve Bank board next meets on August 5.
Figures released earlier on Wednesday showed the consumer price index (CPI) fell 0.2 percent in the June quarter for annual inflation of just 0.3 percent.

They showed also that Australian underlying inflation rose 0.3 percent in the June quarter for an annual rate of 1.7 percent, the lowest annual underlying inflation rate since the series started in 1991.
